questions.text: What command would you use to make the CUPS service persistent at runlevel 3 in SysVinit? (6)
aiRubric: Uses chkconfig for the SysVinit service configuration (2).
Specifies runlevel 3 using --level 3 or an equivalent list that includes 3 (2).
Uses on to enable it persistently (1). Do not require sudo when the answer assumes a root shell.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: These are model study answers, not an official UNISA memorandum. Award partial credit using the rubric. Accept equivalent correct explanations and harmless command-option order changes. The question wording is kept separate from all explanations.
questions.explanation:
CUPS manages printing. A persistent service is configured to start when the system enters the required runlevel.

Why: chkconfig changes the saved SysVinit startup setting. --level 3 chooses the runlevel, cups chooses printing, and on enables its startup. It does not merely start CUPS for the current session.

Student note: Remember the four parts: chkconfig, --level 3, cups, on. Use the init system named in the question.

study.title: CUPS persistence in SysVinit
study.simple: CUPS manages printing. A persistent service is configured to start when the system enters the required runlevel.
whyCorrect: chkconfig changes the saved SysVinit startup setting. --level 3 chooses the runlevel, cups chooses printing, and on enables its startup. It does not merely start CUPS for the current session.
notes: SysVinit uses runlevels to decide which services should run.
Runlevel 3 is normally multi-user text mode with networking in the Red Hat/Fedora course context.
Enabling startup and starting a service now are separate actions.

study.example: To check the saved setting: chkconfig --list cups. To start it immediately: service cups start.
study.pitfall: systemctl is the systemd tool. The question specifically asks for SysVinit.
